To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in the case of a patient with a cardiac arrest due to an acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarct, the heart must be treated first, 2) after percutaneous coronary interventions including anticoagulant medication, the head must be treated first and 3) the head must be investigated first in the case of mild head trauma.

1) PCI is not always the first priority after resuscitation, especially in patients with head trauma; 2) PCI should be postponed in patients with head injury and a normal CT; 3) the risk of a lethal re- haemorrhage is increased in patients with a positive CT and PCI is not always contraindicated; and 4) the risk of re-bleeding is increased in patients on anticoagulants.
In patients with a possible head injury, PCI can be delayed until a negative head CT is available."
